name: Oklahoma

sources.title: Packet OW-2 (Revised 11-2025) -- 2026 Oklahoma Income Tax Withholding Tables
sources.verifiedBy: PDF downloaded directly (curl with a browser User-Agent) and read in full via pdftotext, both WITH and WITHOUT -layout: the -layout extraction shifted the Table of Withholding Allowance Amounts' rows by one payroll frequency (Weekly's row showed Weekly's own $19.23 figure correctly but ALSO Bi-Weekly's $38.46 bleeding into the same visual row) -- resolved by cross-checking against the doc's own prose ('$1,000.00 divided by the number of payroll periods') and its own worked example ('The semi-monthly withholding allowance is $41.67'), both confirming 1,000/N per period exactly. All 8 per-period bracket tables (Tables 1-8) transcribed directly for both Single and Married -- reproduced the Sample Computation Percentage Formula Method example exactly (semi-monthly $1,825, married, 2 allowances: net $1,741.66, bracket [1,129,infinity): $9.10 + 4.5% x $612.66 = $36.6697 -> rounds to $37.00). Caught a real typo in the source's OWN narrative: the worked example's prose says 'The withholding rate is $12.19 plus 4.5%' but then correctly computes using and states the table's real $9.10 base -- the $12.19 figure does not appear anywhere else and was not used. Cross-verified table internal consistency: Married = 2x Single at every boundary and base throughout; Semi-Annual = 2x Quarterly; Annual = 4x Quarterly = 2x Semi-Annual -- all held exactly (to the cent) across all 8 tables.

sources.title: Form OK-W-4 (Rev. 3-2021) -- Employee's State Withholding Allowance Certificate
sources.verifiedBy: PDF downloaded and read directly. Confirms Filing Status has exactly 3 options (Single / Married / Married-but-withhold-at-higher-Single-rate) and that Lines 1-4 (self/spouse/dependents/additional-itemized) sum into ONE undifferentiated allowance count on Line 5 -- unlike Mississippi's differently-valued exemption categories, every OK-W-4 allowance is worth the identical $1,000/year regardless of which line it came from. Line 6 (additional withholding) already works generically via this project's shared certificate.additionalWithholding mechanism. Lines 7/8/9 are THREE textually distinct 'write Exempt' mechanisms (ordinary no-tax-liability exemption; Military Spouses Residency Relief Act; active-duty military income deduction) but all three produce the IDENTICAL mechanical outcome (the employer withholds $0) -- modelled as the single generic certificate.exempt flag rather than three separate fields, since OW-4 itself uses the same word and the same employer-facing action for all three; the legal basis differs only for the employee's own filing obligations, which this engine does not model. The form's own bottom summary ($1,000 personal exemption + $6,350 standard deduction = $7,350 total for Single, doubled for MFJ, +$1,000/dependent) is taxpayer-facing context, not the literal withholding formula -- OW-2's own per-allowance $1,000/N figure is what's actually wired.

sources.title: Oklahoma Statutes Title 68, Section 2358 -- Adjustments to arrive at Oklahoma taxable income and Oklahoma adjusted gross income
sources.verifiedBy: Fetched directly. Quoted: 'For all tax years beginning after December 31, 1981, taxable income and adjusted gross income shall be adjusted to arrive at Oklahoma taxable income and Oklahoma adjusted gross income' -- confirms Oklahoma's own tax base starts from FEDERAL taxable income/AGI, the same evidentiary tier as Louisiana's/Virginia's/West Virginia's/New Mexico's/Hawaii's federal-conformity citations elsewhere in this project (one inferential step removed from the withholding wage base itself, not an itemized 401(k)/125 list).

sources.title: Oklahoma Employment Security Commission -- Important Numbers for Employers 2026
sources.verifiedBy: PDF downloaded and read directly. Quoted verbatim: Taxable Wage Base $25,000.00 (down from $28,200 in 2025); New Employer Tax Rate 1.5%; Range of Rates 0.2% to 5.8% (down from a 0.3%-9.2% range) -- primary-confirmed, matching every secondary source checked with zero discrepancy. Also confirms a genuine, real year-over-year CUT to both the wage base and the rate range for 2026, not just routine indexing.

sources.title: House Bill 2764 bracket restructuring, cross-source confirmation
sources.verifiedBy: Search-synthesized (WebSearch, not independently fetched from the bill text this pass): confirms HB 2764 collapsed Oklahoma's prior 6-bracket individual income tax schedule (0.25%-4.75%) into the 4-bracket schedule (0%/2.5%/3.5%/4.5%) this file's own OW-2 reconstruction independently reproduced -- used as a second, independent corroboration of the bracket COUNT and top rate before trusting the primary document's own tables at face value.

percentageMethod.$comment: OW-2's own Percentage Formula Method: subtract $1,000/allowance/periodsPerYear from period wages, then look up the appropriate per-period 4-bracket table by status. Every allowance (self/spouse/dependent/additional) is worth the identical $1,000/yr -- no per-category dollar differences the way Mississippi has.
percentageMethod.allowanceAmountComment: Each figure is $1,000.00 / periodsPerYear, rounded to the cent -- OW-2's own explicit formula, confirmed exact for every period (1000/52=19.2307->19.23, 1000/26=38.4615->38.46, 1000/24=41.6667->41.67 (matches OW-2's own Sample Computation text verbatim: 'The semi-monthly withholding allowance is $41.67'), 1000/12=83.3333->83.33, 1000/4=250.00, 1000/2=500.00, 1000/1=1000.00, 1000/260=3.8461->3.85).

roundingComment: OW-2 states directly: 'Oklahoma withholding computed using the percentage method must be rounded. Round to the nearest whole dollar by dropping any amount under 50 cents and increasing amounts from 50 to 99 cents to the next higher dollar.' Ordinary round-half-up to the whole dollar -- handled generically via rules.roundFinalToWholeDollar in stateIncomeTax(), the same mechanism built for Maine and reused by Virginia/North Carolina/Mississippi.
exemptPretaxComment: Oklahoma Statutes Title 68 Sec. 2358 confirms Oklahoma taxable income/AGI is adjusted FROM federal taxable income/AGI -- same evidentiary tier as LA/VA/WV/NM/HI's federal-conformity citations, not an itemized 401(k)/125 list.

reciprocity.$comment: CHECKED, not assumed absent: search-synthesized (not independently fetched from an Oklahoma-specific reciprocity statute this pass) -- multiple independent sources agree Oklahoma has no reciprocal withholding agreement with any state.

exemptCertificateNote: OK-W-4 Lines 7/8/9 are three textually distinct 'write Exempt' mechanisms (ordinary no-liability exemption; Military Spouses Residency Relief Act; active-duty military income deduction) collapsed into the single generic certificate.exempt flag -- see the OK-W-4 source note above for why this is a faithful, not a lossy, simplification at the withholding-computation level.

localIncomeTax.rule: NONE. No Oklahoma city or county levies a local income/wage tax.
localIncomeTax.confidence: cross_source_confirmed; not independently verified against a specific municipal-authority statute this pass.

paidFamilyMedicalLeave.rule: NONE mandatory. Oklahoma has no state-run paid family/medical leave program for private employers as of 2026. A tax CREDIT exists for employers who voluntarily provide paid family leave (up to $12,500/qualifying employee against Oklahoma income tax), but this is an employer income-tax credit, not a payroll withholding mechanism -- correctly out of scope for this engine.
paidFamilyMedicalLeave.confidence: cross_source_confirmed via search synthesis, not independently fetched from a specific enacted statute this pass.

unemploymentInsurance.confidence: primary_source_confirmed -- oklahoma.gov's own 2026 Employer Important Numbers PDF, quoted directly above.
unemploymentInsurance.note: A genuine year-over-year CUT for 2026: wage base down from $28,200 (2025) to $25,000, rate range down from 0.3%-9.2% to 0.2%-5.8%.
unemploymentInsurance.knownGap: This state's UI rate is experience-rated -- an individual employer's actual rate depends on employer-specific history a static jurisdiction file can't hold, which is why stateUnemploymentEmployerTax() (src/taxes/state.ts) takes the caller-supplied rate (input.employer.stateUnemploymentRate) when given. STILL OPEN: whether this state's unemployment wage base excludes the same pretax categories as its income tax withholding (the engine currently applies exemptPretax to both) — elective deferrals are commonly included in the unemployment base while excluded from income tax.

knownGaps: Supplemental wages: OW-2's full text was checked for a separate flat supplemental rate (searched 'supplemental') and none was found -- Oklahoma appears to use ordinary aggregation like several other states in this project, not modelled as a distinct method since there's nothing distinct to model.

Local-tax absence: CLOSED 2026-09-02, but with an important nuance the prior 'cross-source only' phrasing missed -- unlike states with a categorical constitutional bar, Oklahoma's own municipal-taxation statute (68 O.S. Section 2701, 'Authorization to tax for purposes of municipal government') actually GRANTS incorporated cities and towns broad power to 'assess, levy, and collect taxes for general and special purposes of municipal government as the Legislature may levy and collect for purposes of state government' (i.e. this legal authority could in principle extend to a local income/payroll/earnings tax on residents) -- the statute's only explicit restriction is that 'no earnings, payroll or income taxes may be levied on nonresidents of the cities or towns levying such tax.' So the correct disclosure is: no OK municipality currently exercises this authority (cross-source confirmed across Symmetry's payroll-tax-system research, Paylocity, OnPay -- no city or county wage/payroll tax is withheld anywhere in the state as of 2026, including Oklahoma City and Tulsa), not that one is legally impossible the way Louisiana's constitution forecloses it. If any OK municipality ever enacts one under 2701's authority, it could only apply to its own residents, never nonresident commuters. Reciprocity absence: CLOSED 2026-09-02, primary-source confirmed -- fetched the Oklahoma Tax Commission's own Form 511-TX ('Credit for Tax Paid to Another State,' oklahoma.gov/.../511-TX.pdf) directly, which cites its statutory basis explicitly as '68 Oklahoma Statutes Section 2357(B)(1) and Rule 710:50-15-72.' This is OK's mechanism for resolving double taxation on residents who work in another state: report the income on the OK return, then claim a credit for tax paid to that other state, capped at the OK-attributable proportion. Critically, the form states plainly under 'Who Does Not Qualify?': 'A nonresident taxpayer does not qualify for this credit' -- and the credit mechanism applies uniformly to income earned in 'another state' with no state-specific carve-out anywhere in the form or its instructions for any partner/reciprocal state. A genuine reciprocity agreement would make this credit unnecessary for that partner state's residents (their wages would simply be exempt from withholding at the source under the compact, not taxed-then-credited) -- the credit method's universal, unexception'd application across all fifty states is itself the primary-source proof that Oklahoma has zero reciprocal withholding agreements: if OK had reciprocity with any state, that state's wage-earners wouldn't need this credit at all. Combined with OW-2's own total silence on residency/reciprocity (checked across all 20 pages of the 2026 edition -- no mention of 'nonresident' or 'other state'), this closes the gap: OK's uniform reliance on the credit method, confirmed by its own tax form's cited statute, is the primary-source evidence of no reciprocity, not merely an absence of a document saying so.

STILL OPEN: whether this state's unemployment wage base excludes the same pretax categories as its income tax withholding (the engine currently applies exemptPretax to both) — elective deferrals are commonly included in the unemployment base while excluded from income tax.

Wage Bracket Tables (the simpler lookup-table alternative to the Percentage Formula Method, pages 10+ of OW-2) were not transcribed -- OW-2 itself states both methods 'produce almost identical results'; this file wires the Percentage Formula Method only, consistent with this project's standing preference for formula methods over bracket-table transcription when both are offered.

suiEmployer.$comment: Normalized employer-side unemployment parameters — the shape src/taxes/state.ts reads. The detailed unemploymentInsurance block above stays the record of research; this exists because that block's shape varies too much between states to compute from directly (wage bases as objects, industry-keyed rate maps, differently-named keys).
suiEmployer.wageBaseSource: 2026 taxable wage bases cross-checked against EY's published 2026 state-by-state table; where this file already carried a numeric wage base, the two agreed unless noted in wageBaseNote.
suiEmployer.newEmployerRateSource: This state's own unemploymentInsurance block above, researched in an earlier pass — kept in preference to any aggregate table.
